priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against a limited historical surgery health-and-net-resource channel; not portfolio EV or a marginal gift price.

what: TOMAGWA provides medical, dental, vision, pharmacy and related care for people with limited resources around Tomball and greater Houston.
It became a federally qualified health center look-alike in 2024 and serves uninsured patients alongside Medicare and Medicaid patients.
Federal reporting identifies 118 oral-surgery patients in 2024; other services are not included in this narrow health illustration.
strengths: Original FY2024 costs and separately dated federal surgery outcomes remain preserved.
Current sliding-fee and insurance sources support financial-protection and access-cost mechanisms without retail-value income claims.
The revised initial model exposes health and signed resources, full unsuccessful-care burdens and distinct payer uncertainty.
reservations: The 118 surgery patients are a historical 2024 partial channel, not the whole portfolio or current gift-created capacity.
Clinical utility, otherwise-paid cash, household grouping, net access costs and local share are transparent judgments, not local causal measurements.
Public and insured alternatives, outside payer resources and omitted broad services could materially change the conditional result.

sections.what: TOMAGWA provides comprehensive primary and dental care, pharmacy, vision, laboratory and case-management services. Current locations include Tomball and Champions in Houston, with mobile delivery across Greater Houston and Harris County. Its 2024 Form 990 identifies TOMAGWA Ministries Inc DBA TOMAGWA HealthCare Ministries, EIN 76-0280324, and February 2024 FQHC Look-Alike designation. Look-Alike status is not proof of federal Section 330 funding. [Recipient site](https://www.tomagwa.org/) [Original filing](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349321450/IRS990)
sections.monitoring: The 2024 HRSA return counts 1,965 patients overall and 118 oral-surgery patients with 131 surgery visits (Table6A DJ97 and DI97). In 2025 the corresponding surgery counts are 135 patients and 240 visits. These are reported treatment-category patients, not observed incremental cures. Restorative and examination patients can overlap and receive no added modeled credit. The 2024 tax filing repeats a 2023 narrative of 18,326 dental services; that is neither 2024 activity nor a unique-patient count. [2024 UDS](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/LAL-2024.xlsx) [2025 UDS](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/LAL-2025.xlsx)
sections.qualitative: Care reaches a population with limited resources and plausible unmet need. The 2024 federal ZIP rows place 1,758 patients in named Houston-metro ZIP areas; 28 are in Plantersville/Grimes, 156 in other ZIPs, and some small cells are suppressed. This is overall patient residence, not surgery-specific health attribution. A Swedish prospective cohort compared root canals with extraction and found no significant intergroup QALY difference; it does not identify the benefit of TOMAGWA surgery over alternative care. The model therefore labels utility, relief and duration as priors. [Needs assessment](https://www.tomagwa.org/_files/ugd/a79649_a42ddabd7ed84d0ca420cfde6c9a8ff0.pdf) [Clinical study](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cre2.759) The current sliding-fee source requires a nominal payment and permits insured patients to apply; the patient page lists Medicaid, Medicare and private plans. These are actual alternatives and payment mechanisms, not evidence every surgery patient is uninsured or avoids a retail bill.
sections.cost: The original $43.77M health-only estimate is preserved as a diagnostic. The revised conditional annual reference is about $24.28M per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: .94116 clinical years plus .07662 signed resource equivalents. It removes the .6 gift-capacity multiplier from an annual-work comparison and retains full .05 clinical harm, then explicitly assesses net household resources; this is a scope/accounting judgment revision, not observed improved performance. Full FY2024 $2,471,560 remains compared with only 118 surgery patients, so this is neither complete portfolio EV nor next-gift productivity. Other services remain unquantified, not zero. No observed surgery cost allocation was located: the .2 cost-allocation sensitivity is explicitly hypothetical; $2,023,642 is all recognized program spending, not surgery spending. $476,624 extra volunteer resources remain only a sensitivity, not observed FY2024 costs.
sections.funding: Donor HOLD. TRHF approved $595,000 of 2024 dental funding and described a $400,000 February–December 2025 contract; these are existing funding, not open gift gaps. UDS also reports local government and private grants. Current clinician capacity, 2026 grant renewal, restrictions and the response to a new gift need verification. The official giving form permits ordinary gifts but prices no additional surgery. [2024 funding approval](https://trhfoundation.org/images/pdfs/financials/minutes/20231129_THA_Board_Minutes_Signed.pdf) [2025 contract minutes](https://trhfoundation.org/2025-board-minutes/158-february-19-2025-1) [Give](https://www.tomagwa.org/donate) Signed resources are assessed separately from clinical response: .8 households per surgery patient and .6 incremental affordable-access share are judged; $200 otherwise-paid medical cash avoidance receives .5 positive-overlap reduction, while $25 net additional fees/time/access costs are fully retained on every exposed household. Earnings centrally remain zero; positive/negative net-work cases are hypotheses, not child or survivor wages. Changed-household gains and costs enter one log in the same year against judged $20,000 resources. Cash avoidance is after existing coverage, not retail charity-care value. The central donor-budget convention includes no extra outside payer loss; full-transfer and additional-provider-resource cases explicitly challenge that convention. Costs and process harms survive unsuccessful benefits. Unknown resource and clinical-null/adverse cases remain visible. The original tracked acceptance is docs/houston-tomagwa-alpha-acceptance.md; this revision independently re-reviews signed annual-channel accounting, not all underlying historical source collection.

model.costScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against a limited historical surgery health-and-net-resource channel; not portfolio EV or a marginal gift price.
model.geographicAttribution: 2024 ZIP rows and CHNA county mapping establish actual Houston reach. Central 93% benefit share is a judgment; surgical cohort geography is unknown and some ZIP areas cross counties.
model.formula: Clinical = (patient N × symptomatic successful share × incremental relief × utility × finite years − full process harm) × local share. Household resources use N × unique; changed = households × incremental affordable-access share. Joint household gain minus full cost enters .5 × people × years × log(after/before); only positive benefits discounted for overlap. Distinct payer losses for local recipients included globally once. Price = 10C/(clinical + signed income equivalents) when positive; no separate donor multiplier on annual work.
model.counterfactual: Other dental providers, public/payer coverage and existing TRHF contracts can substitute for ordinary-gift support. Symptom success, additional relief and funding response are separately explicit priors.
model.attribution: Annual clinical treatment response and relief beyond alternatives retained as judgments; gift expansion response is separate unknown capacity, not a second annual welfare multiplier. Health patients distinct from household grouping. Financial access not gated by symptom relief.
model.uncertainty: Very low confidence in health and donation attribution. Scenarios are illustrative, not confidence intervals; no calibrated probabilities or expected-value estimate. Null and adverse are viable. Net cash and time costs are explicitly judged, with zero/negative/unknown and outside-payer cases. Current fee mechanisms cannot establish the amount of surgery savings.
model.nativeOutcomes: Reported oral-surgery patients, discounted for symptomatic successful treatment and relief beyond alternative care, with finite utility duration and harm.
